_strings.@@b6c075bbc728: Treaty conformity — LA conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from LA income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the LA return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: LA's resident return (IT-540) starts from Federal Adjusted Gross Income: Line 7 is "FEDERAL ADJUSTED GROSS INCOME" and the instructions say "Line 7 - Enter the amount of your Federal Adjusted Gross Income (Federal AGI). This amount is taken from Federal Form 1040 or 1040-SR, Line 11." Federally treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI (Form 1040 Line 11) and therefore flows through. The only "additions" to federal AGI are on Schedule E, Lines 2A-2D: (2A) interest and dividend income from other states and their political subdivisions, (2B) recapture of START contributions, (2C) recapture of START K12 contributions, and (2D) add-back of pass-through entity loss. There is NO add-back of tax-treaty-exempt income anywhere on the IT-540 form, Schedule E, or in the instructions (the word "treaty" appears zero times in both the 2023 IT-540 form PDF and the 2023 IT-540 instructions PDF). Because LA starts from federal AGI and has no treaty addback, treaty-exempt income is not re-taxed -> conforms.
_strings.@@b73fe32d7a7f: Louisiana School Readiness Child Care Expense Credit (refundable, federal AGI $25,000 or less) — Taxpayers who qualify for the Louisiana Child Care Credit and who had a qualified dependent under age six that attended a child care facility participating in the Quality Start Rating program (administered by the Louisiana Dept. of Education) rated at two stars or higher. Facility must provide Form R-10614. Refundable version requires federal AGI of $25,000 or less. Authorized by R.S. 47:6104.

Instructions, Line 10: "Use the tax table that corresponds with your filing status. Locate the amount of your tax table income from Line 9 in the first two columns of the tax table. Read across to the column numbered the same as the total number of exemptions claimed on Line 6F. The amount shown in that column is your Louisiana tax liability. ... If you have more than 8 exemptions, refer to the instructions at the top of the tax tables." Verified exemption kinds shipped but NOT applied by this op (compute them on the form): age_65 ($1,000 — $1,000 per '65 or older' box marked on IT-540 Lines 6A/6B (taxpayer and spouse each), counted in the Line 6F exemption total and deducted from the lowest bracket via the tax table column. NOT applied by calc.state_tax - claim it on the form through the Line 6F exemption count.); blind ($1,000 — $1,000 per 'Blind' box marked on IT-540 Lines 6A/6B (taxpayer and spouse each), counted in the Line 6F exemption total and deducted from the lowest bracket via the tax table column. NOT applied by calc.state_tax - claim it on the form through the Line 6F exemption count.) Pack notes: Base guidance: Supply 2023 Form IT-540, Line 9: "YOUR LOUISIANA TAX TABLE INCOME - Subtract Line 8D from Line 7. If less than zero, enter '0.'" Line 7 is Federal Adjusted Gross Income (Federal Form 1040/1040-SR, Line 11; if less than zero enter 0; if you have Louisiana additions/exempt income, Line 7 comes from Louisiana Schedule E, Line 5 instead). Line 8D, "EXCESS FEDERAL ITEMIZED DEDUCTIONS," applies only to federal itemizers and equals Line 8B (federal itemized deduction for medical and dental expenses, federal Schedule A Line 4) minus Line 8C (federal standard deduction: $13,850 statuses 1/3, $27,700 statuses 2/5, $20,800 status 4), floor zero. IMPORTANT: supply Line 9 UNREDUCED - do NOT subtract Louisiana's $4,500/$9,000 combined personal exemption-standard deduction yourself; it is encoded in the zero-rate bottom bracket shipped here (standard_deduction is null for that reason). Adjudication note (two-pass): base is federal_agi — IT-540 Line 7 is federal adjusted gross income and Line 9 tax table income derives from it (see base-quirk note); supply Line 9. exemptions_count must be 0: the primary personal exemptions are BUILT INTO the zero-rate floor ($4,500 single/MFS; $9,000 MFJ/QSS and Head of Household per the printed table headers), never subtracted separately. Table mandate below $51,000 ($101,000 for MFJ/QSS): IT-540 Line 10 requires taking the tax from the printed 2023 Louisiana Tax Table for your filing status and Line 6F exemption count - bracket math may differ by a few dollars within table bands (the printed cells equal bracket math evaluated at the midpoint of each $250 income band in every cell sampled); the filed form must use the table. Louisiana has NO separate standard-deduction or exemption subtraction line on the IT-540: a combined personal exemption-standard deduction of $4,500 (Single, MFS) or $9,000 (MFJ, QSS, HOH) is built into the tax tables and, per the 2023 IT-540B Tax Computation Worksheet (nonresident instructions p. 4, the only 2023 LDR document that prints the rates explicitly), it is deducted from income taxed in the LOWEST (1.85%) bracket - not from the top of income. It is therefore shipped here as the zero-rate bottom bracket, and standard_deduction is null: supply Line 9 tax table income unreduced and do not subtract $4,500/$9,000 yourself. Statutory bracket boundaries ($12,500/$50,000; $25,000/$100,000 for statuses 2 and 5) are unchanged. Above the table cap, the table itself prescribes 'Plus 4.25% of Tax Table Income in Excess of $51,000' ($101,000 MFJ/QSS) added to the last printed row, which was computed at that band's midpoint ($50,875/$100,875) - the official method therefore comes out about $5 below exact bracket math (e.g., Single, one exemption, Line 9 exactly $51,000: table method $1,498 vs bracket math $1,503). Qualifying Surviving Spouse (filing status 5) shares the Married Filing Jointly tax table, brackets, and $9,000 combined deduction - the engine's QSS -> married_filing_jointly mapping is exact. Head of Household shares the Single/MFS bracket boundaries ($12,500/$50,000) but gets the $9,000 combined personal exemption-standard deduction ($4,500 more than Single) - hence its different zero-rate floor. The zero-rate floor covers only the base exemption count (one exemption for Single/MFS/HOH; two for MFJ/QSS - the MFJ/QSS table has no one-exemption column, and Line 6 requires the same exemptions as your federal return except for the dependent-on-another's-return, 65-or-over, and blind cases). Every additional Line 6F exemption ($1,000 each - dependents, 65-or-over boxes, blind boxes) is handled per the shipped 'dependent'/'age_65'/'blind' entries and their noted engine divergence. Louisiana credits are NOT modeled by this op and come off after Line 10: Nonrefundable Priority 1 credits (Schedule C) on Line 11; refundable child care credit (federal AGI <= $25,000), refundable school readiness credit, and the Louisiana Earned Income Credit (5% of the federal EIC) on Lines 13-15; other refundable Priority 2/4 credits (Schedules F and I) and nonrefundable Priority 3 credits including the nonrefundable child care credit (Schedule J) on Lines 16/20/25. Base quirk (affects the figure you supply, not this computation): Louisiana's only deduction between federal AGI and tax table income is Line 8D 'EXCESS FEDERAL ITEMIZED DEDUCTIONS' = federal itemized MEDICAL AND DENTAL deduction (Schedule A Line 4) minus the federal standard deduction, floor zero, for federal itemizers only - since tax year 2022 no other federal itemized excess is deductible; non-itemizers leave Lines 8A-8D blank.
